I farm the way I know best: steady, careful, and not too risky. I am 79 years old, my land is only 4.1 mu, and there are just 2 people in my household, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all my land and use methods that are familiar, reliable, and not too labor-demanding. I have well irrigation, so I will use it at the key stages instead of depending only on rain. For wheat, I will use improved seed because it is more stable than old seed and easier for me to manage than taking chances. I will put enough nitrogen for strong growth, with moderate phosphorus and potassium, and irrigate several times because wheat here needs water at the important stages. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor compared with deep ploughing and still prepares the field well on my small plot. For maize, I will also plant all 4.1 mu after wheat harvest. I will use hybrid seed because maize gives better yield that way. I will fertilize, but not excessively, because I want stable output and do not want to waste money. I will irrigate fewer times than wheat, and I will spray pesticides only when needed, mainly to protect against common field pests and diseases. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield. I will manage for a dependable harvest, lower labor pressure, and less risk.
